readings.title: The Torah of Childbirth
readings.subtitle: Cleansing After Birth
readings.text:
[Leviticus 12:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying,
[2] <dq>Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘When a woman has conceived, and has given birth to <dn>את</dn> a male child, then she shall be unclean seven days, as in the days of her monthly separation she is unclean.</dq>
[3] <dq>‘And on the eighth day <dn>את</dn> the flesh of his foreskin is circumcised.</dq>
[4] <dq>‘And she remains in the blood of her cleansing thirty-three days. She does not touch whatever is set-apart, and she does not come into the set-apart place until the days of her cleansing are completed.</dq>
[5] <dq>‘But if she gives birth to a female child, then she shall be unclean for two weeks, as in her monthly separation, and she remains in the blood of her cleansing for sixty-six days.</dq>
[6] <dq>‘And when the days of her cleansing are completed, for a son or for a daughter, she brings to the priest a lamb a year old, as an ascending offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering, to the door of the Tent of Appointment.</dq>
[7] <dq>‘And he shall bring it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed from the flow of her blood. This is the Torah for her who has given birth to a male or a female.</dq>
[8] <dq>‘And if she is not able to bring a lamb, then she shall bring <dn>את</dn> two turtledoves or <dn>את</dn> two young pigeons, one as an ascending offering and the other as a sin offering. And the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.’</dq> ”

readings.title: The Torah of Leprosy
readings.subtitle: Diagnosing Skin Infections
readings.text:
[Leviticus 13:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
[2] <dq>When a man has on the skin of his body a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot, and it shall become on the skin of his body like a leprous infection, then he shall be brought to Aharon the priest or to one of his sons the priests.</dq>
[3] <dq>And the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> the infection on the skin of the body. And if the hair on the infection has turned white, and the infection appears to be deeper than the skin of his body, it is a leprous infection. And the priest shall look at him, and pronounce <dn>את</dn> him unclean.</dq>
[4] <dq>But if the bright spot is white on the skin of his body, and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, then the priest shall shut up <dn>את</dn> the infected one seven days.</dq>
[5] <dq>And the priest shall look at him on the seventh day and see, if the infection appears to be as it was, and the infection has not spread on the skin, then the priest shall shut him up another seven days.</dq>
[6] <dq>And the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> him again on the seventh day and see, if the infection has darkened, and the infection has not spread on the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. It is a scab, and he shall wash his garments and be clean.</dq>
[7] <dq>But if the scab spreads further over the skin, after he has been seen by the priest for his cleansing, he shall be seen by the priest again.</dq>
[8] <dq>And the priest shall look and see, if the scab has spread on the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean, it is leprosy.</dq>
[9] <dq>When the infection of leprosy is on a man, then he shall be brought to the priest.</dq>
[10] <dq>And the priest shall look and see, if the swelling on the skin is white, and it has turned the hair white, and there is a spot of raw flesh in the swelling,</dq>
[11] <dq>it is an old leprosy on the skin of his body, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. He does not shut him up, for he is unclean.</dq>
[12] <dq>And if leprosy breaks out all over the skin, and the leprosy shall cover <dn>את</dn> all the skin of the infected one, from his head to his foot, wherever the priest looks,</dq>
[13] <dq>then the priest shall look and see, if the leprosy has covered <dn>את</dn> all his body, he shall pronounce <dn>את</dn> the infected one clean. It has all turned white, he is clean.</dq>
[14] <dq>But the day raw flesh appears on him, he is unclean.</dq>
[15] <dq>And the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> the raw flesh and pronounce him to be unclean – the raw flesh is unclean, it is leprosy.</dq>
[16] <dq>Or when the raw flesh changes and turns white again, he shall come to the priest.</dq>
[17] <dq>And the priest shall look at him and see, if the infection has turned white, then the priest shall pronounce <dn>את</dn> the infected one clean, he is clean.</dq>
[18] <dq>And when the body has a boil in the skin, and it is healed,</dq>
[19] <dq>and in the place of the boil there comes a white swelling or a bright spot, reddish-white, then it shall be seen by the priest.</dq>
[20] <dq>And the priest shall look and see, if it appears deeper than the skin, and its hair has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean, it is a leprous infection which has broken out of the boil.</dq>
[21] <dq>But if the priest looks at it and sees no white hairs in it, and it is not deeper than the skin, but has faded, then the priest shall shut him up seven days;</dq>
[22] <dq>and if it has spread further over the skin, then the priest shall pronounce <dn>את</dn> him unclean, it is a leprous infection.</dq>
[23] <dq>But if the bright spot stays in its place, it has not spread, it is the scar of the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.</dq>
[24] <dq>Or when the body receives a burn on its skin by fire, and the raw flesh of the burn shall become a bright spot, reddish-white or white,</dq>
[25] <dq>then the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> it and see, if the hair of the bright spot has turned white, and it appears deeper than the skin, it is leprosy broken out in the burn. And the priest shall pronounce <dn>את</dn> him unclean, it is a leprous infection.</dq>
[26] <dq>But if the priest looks at it and sees there are no white hairs in the bright spot, and it is not deeper than the skin, but has faded, then the priest shall shut him up seven days.</dq>
[27] <dq>And the priest shall look at him on the seventh day. If it spreads further over the skin, then the priest shall pronounce <dn>את</dn> him unclean, it is a leprous infection.</dq>
[28] <dq>But if the bright spot stays in its place, and has not spread on the skin, but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn. And the priest shall pronounce him clean, for it is the scar from the burn.</dq>
[29] <dq>And when a man, or a woman, has an infection on the head or in the beard,</dq>
[30] <dq>then the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> the infection and see, if it appears deeper than the skin, and there is thin yellow hair in it, then the priest shall pronounce <dn>את</dn> him unclean, it is an eruption, a leprosy of the head or beard.</dq>
[31] <dq>But when the priest looks at <dn>את</dn> the infection of the eruption and sees that it does not appear deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, then the priest shall shut up <dn>את</dn> the one with the infection of the eruption seven days.</dq>
[32] <dq>And on the seventh day the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> the infection and see, if the eruption has not spread, and there is no yellow hair in it, and the eruption does not appear deeper than the skin,</dq>
[33] <dq>then he shall shave himself, but <dn>את</dn> the eruption he does not shave. And the priest shall shut up <dn>את</dn> the one with the eruption another seven days.</dq>
[34] <dq>And on the seventh day the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> the eruption and see, if the eruption has not spread over the skin, and does not appear deeper than the skin, then the priest shall pronounce <dn>את</dn> him clean. And he shall wash his garments, and he shall be clean.</dq>
[35] <dq>But if the eruption spreads further over the skin after his cleansing,</dq>
[36] <dq>then the priest shall look at him and see, if the eruption has spread over the skin, the priest need not seek for yellow hair, he is unclean.</dq>
[37] <dq>But if the eruption appears to have stayed, and there is black hair grown up in it, the eruption has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.</dq>
[38] <dq>And when a man or a woman has bright spots on the skin of the body, white bright spots,</dq>
[39] <dq>then the priest shall look and see, if the bright spots on the skin of the body are dull white, it is a white spot that grows on the skin, he is clean.</dq>
[40] <dq>And when a man loses the hair of his head, he is bald, he is clean.</dq>
[41] <dq>And if the hair has fallen from his forehead, he is bald on the forehead, he is clean.</dq>
[42] <dq>And when there is on the bald head or bald forehead a reddish-white infection, it is leprosy breaking out on his bald head or his bald forehead.</dq>
[43] <dq>And the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> it and see, if the swelling of the infection is reddish-white on his bald head or on his bald forehead, as the appearance of leprosy on the skin of the body,</dq>
[44] <dq>he is a leprous man, he is unclean. The priest shall pronounce him unclean, without fail, his infection is on his head.</dq>
[45] <dq>As for the leper who has the infection, his garments are torn, and his head is uncovered, and he has to cover his upper lip and cry, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’</dq>
[46] <dq>He is unclean – all the days he has the infection he is unclean. He is unclean, and he dwells alone, his dwelling place is outside the camp.</dq>

readings.title: Leprosy in Garments
readings.subtitle: Cleansing and Burning
readings.text:
[Leviticus 13:47] <dq>And when a garment has an infection of leprosy in it, in a woollen garment or in a linen garment,</dq>
[48] <dq>or in the warp or in the weft of linen or wool, or in leather or in any leather-work,</dq>
[49] <dq>and the infection shall be greenish or reddish in the garment or in the leather, or in the warp or in the weft, or in any leather object, it is an infection of leprosy and shall be shown to <dn>את</dn> the priest.</dq>
[50] <dq>And the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> the infection and shut up <dn>את</dn> the infected seven days.</dq>
[51] <dq>And he shall look at <dn>את</dn> the infection on the seventh day. And when the infection has spread in the garment, or in the warp or in the weft, or in the leather or any leather-work, the infection is an active leprosy, it is unclean.</dq>
[52] <dq>And he shall burn <dn>את</dn> that garment, or <dn>את</dn> the warp or <dn>את</dn> the weft, in wool or in linen, or <dn>את</dn> any leather object in which the infection is, for it is an active leprosy. It is burned with fire.</dq>
[53] <dq>But if the priest looks and sees that the infection has not spread in the garment, or in the warp or in the weft, or in any leather object,</dq>
[54] <dq>then the priest shall give command, and they shall wash <dn>את</dn> that in which the infection is. And he shall shut it up another seven days.</dq>
[55] <dq>And the priest shall look at <dn>את</dn> the infection after it has been washed and see, if the infection has not changed <dn>את</dn> its appearance, though the infection has not spread, it is unclean, and burn it in the fire – it is eaten away, in its inside or outside.</dq>
[56] <dq>And if the priest shall look and see that the infection has faded after washing <dn>את</dn> it, then he shall tear <dn>את</dn> it out of the garment, or out of the warp, or out of the weft, or out of the leather.</dq>
[57] <dq>And if it is still seen in the garment, or in the warp or in the weft, or in any leather object, it is a spreading infection. Burn it with fire, <dn>את</dn> that in which the infection is.</dq>
[58] <dq>And if you wash the garment, or the warp or the weft, or any leather object, if the infection has disappeared from it, then it shall be washed a second time, and shall be clean.</dq>
[59] <dq>This is the Torah of the infection of leprosy in a garment of wool or linen, or in the warp or in the weft, or in any leather object, to pronounce it clean or to pronounce it unclean.</dq>”

readings.title: The Cleansing of the Leper
readings.subtitle: The Ritual of Restoration
readings.text:
[Leviticus 14:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying,
[2] <dq>This shall be the Torah of the leper for the day of his cleansing: He shall be brought to the priest,</dq>
[3] <dq>and the priest shall go out of the camp, and the priest shall look and see, if the leprosy is healed in the leper,</dq>
[4] <dq>then the priest shall command, and he shall take for him who is to be cleansed two live and clean birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.</dq>
[5] <dq>And the priest shall command, and he shall slay <dn>את</dn> one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water.</dq>
[6] <dq>Let him take <dn>את</dn> the live bird and <dn>את</dn> the cedar wood and <dn>את</dn> the scarlet and <dn>את</dn> the hyssop, and dip <dn>את</dn> them and <dn>את</dn> the live bird in the blood of the bird that was slain over the running water.</dq>
[7] <dq>And he shall sprinkle it seven times on him who is to be cleansed from the leprosy, and shall pronounce him clean, and shall let <dn>את</dn> the live bird loose in the open field.</dq>
[8] <dq>And he who is to be cleansed shall wash <dn>את</dn> his garments, and shall shave off <dn>את</dn> all his hair and wash himself in water, and shall be clean. Then after that he comes into the camp, but shall stay outside his tent seven days.</dq>
[9] <dq>And on the seventh day it shall be that he shaves <dn>את</dn> all the hair off <dn>את</dn> his head and <dn>את</dn> his beard and <dn>את</dn> his eyebrows, even <dn>את</dn> all his hair he shaves off. And he shall wash <dn>את</dn> his garments and wash <dn>את</dn> his body in water, and shall be clean.</dq>
[10] <dq>And on the eighth day he takes two male lambs, perfect ones, and one ewe lamb a year old, a perfect one, and three-tenths of an ěphah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and one log of oil.</dq>
[11] <dq>And the priest who is cleansing shall present <dn>את</dn> the man who is to be cleansed, with <dn>את</dn> these offerings, before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, at the door of the Tent of Appointment.</dq>
[12] <dq>And the priest shall take <dn>את</dn> one male lamb and bring <dn>את</dn> it as a guilt offering, and <dn>את</dn> the log of oil, and wave <dn>את</dn> them as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[13] <dq>And he shall slay <dn>את</dn> the lamb in the place where he slays <dn>את</dn> the sin offering and <dn>את</dn> the ascending offering, in a set-apart place. For the guilt offering, like the sin offering, belongs to the priest. It is most set-apart.</dq>
[14] <dq>And the priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering, and the priest shall put it on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.</dq>
[15] <dq>And the priest shall take some of the log of oil, and pour it into the palm of his own left hand.</dq>
[16] <dq>And the priest shall dip <dn>את</dn> his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[17] <dq>And of the rest of the oil in his hand, the priest puts some on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the blood of the guilt offering.</dq>
[18] <dq>And the rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he puts on the head of him who is to be cleansed. And the priest shall make atonement for him before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[19] <dq>And the priest shall make <dn>את</dn> the sin offering, and make atonement for him who is to be cleansed from his uncleanness. Then afterwards he slays <dn>את</dn> the ascending offering.</dq>
[20] <dq>And the priest shall offer <dn>את</dn> the ascending offering and <dn>את</dn> the grain offering on the slaughter-place. And the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.</dq>
[21] <dq>But if he is poor and is unable to afford it, then he shall take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, and one-tenth of an ěphah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and a log of oil,</dq>
[22] <dq>and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, such as he is able to afford, and one shall be a sin offering and the other an ascending offering.</dq>
[23] <dq>And he shall bring <dn>את</dn> them to the priest on the eighth day for his cleansing, to the door of the Tent of Appointment, before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[24] <dq>And the priest shall take <dn>את</dn> the lamb of the guilt offering and <dn>את</dn> the log of oil, and the priest shall wave <dn>את</dn> them as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[25] <dq>And he shall slay <dn>את</dn> the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.</dq>
[26] <dq>Then the priest pours some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand.</dq>
[27] <dq>And the priest shall sprinkle with his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[28] <dq>And the priest shall put some of the oil that is in his hand on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of the right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the place of the blood of the guilt offering.</dq>
[29] <dq>And the rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he puts on the head of him who is to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[30] <dq>And he shall prepare <dn>את</dn> one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, such as he is able to afford,</dq>
[31] <dq><dn>את</dn> that which he is able to afford, <dn>את</dn> the one as a sin offering and <dn>את</dn> the other as an ascending offering, with the grain offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him who is to be cleansed before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[32] <dq>This is the Torah for one who had an infection of leprosy, who is unable to afford for his cleansing.</dq>”

readings.title: Leprosy in Houses
readings.subtitle: The Plague in the Walls
readings.text:
[Leviticus 14:33] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
[34] <dq>When you come into the land of Kena‛an, which <dn>I</dn> am giving you as a possession, and <dn>I</dn> put a plague of leprosy in a house in the land of your possession,</dq>
[35] <dq>then shall the one who owns the house come and inform the priest, saying, ‘It seems to me that there is some plague in the house.’</dq>
[36] <dq>And the priest shall command, and they shall empty <dn>את</dn> the house, before the priest goes in to look at <dn>את</dn> the plague, so that all that is in the house is not made unclean. And after that the priest goes in to look at <dn>את</dn> the house.</dq>
[37] <dq>And he shall look at <dn>את</dn> the plague and see, if the plague is on the walls of the house with sunken places, greenish or reddish, which appear to be deep in the wall,</dq>
[38] <dq>then the priest shall go out of the house, to the door of the house, and shut up <dn>את</dn> the house seven days.</dq>
[39] <dq>And the priest shall come again on the seventh day and look and see, if the plague has spread on the walls of the house,</dq>
[40] <dq>then the priest shall command, and they shall remove <dn>את</dn> the stones with the plague in them, and they shall throw <dn>את</dn> them outside the city, into an unclean place,</dq>
[41] <dq>while he lets <dn>את</dn> the house be scraped inside, all around, and <dn>את</dn> the dust that they scrape off they shall pour out in an unclean place outside the city.</dq>
[42] <dq>And they shall take other stones and put them in the place of those stones, and take other mortar and plaster <dn>את</dn> the house.</dq>
[43] <dq>And if the plague comes back and breaks out in the house, after he has removed <dn>את</dn> the stones, after he has scraped <dn>את</dn> the house, and after it is plastered,</dq>
[44] <dq>then the priest shall come and look and see, if the plague has spread in the house, it is an active leprosy in the house, it is unclean.</dq>
[45] <dq>And he shall break down <dn>את</dn> the house, <dn>את</dn> its stones, and <dn>את</dn> its timber, and <dn>את</dn> all the plaster of the house, and he shall bring them outside the city to an unclean place.</dq>
[46] <dq>And he who goes into the house, all the days while it is shut up, becomes unclean until evening.</dq>
[47] <dq>And he who lies down in the house has to wash <dn>את</dn> his garments, and he who eats in the house has to wash <dn>את</dn> his garments.</dq>
[48] <dq>However, if the priest indeed comes in and looks at it and sees that the plague has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, then the priest shall pronounce <dn>את</dn> the house clean, because the plague is healed.</dq>
[49] <dq>And to cleanse <dn>את</dn> the house, he shall take two birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.</dq>
[50] <dq>And he shall slay <dn>את</dn> one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water,</dq>
[51] <dq>and he shall take <dn>את</dn> the cedar wood, and <dn>את</dn> the hyssop, and <dn>את</dn> the scarlet, and <dn>את</dn> the live bird, and dip <dn>את</dn> them in the blood of the slain bird and in the running water, and shall sprinkle the house seven times.</dq>
[52] <dq>He shall thus cleanse <dn>את</dn> the house with the blood of the bird and the running water and the live bird, and with the cedar wood, and with the hyssop, and with the scarlet,</dq>
[53] <dq>and he shall let <dn>את</dn> the live bird loose outside the city in the open field, and shall make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.</dq>
[54] <dq>This is the Torah for any infection of leprosy, and eruption,</dq>
[55] <dq>and for leprosy of a garment, and of a house,</dq>
[56] <dq>and for a swelling, and for a scab, and for a bright spot,</dq>
[57] <dq>to teach when it is unclean and when it is clean. This is the Torah of leprosy.</dq>”
